scope: Original SMB3 Mapper 4 implementation, menu import, local Keil build, and execution of the real ARM AXF under Unicorn

hardware.note: No firmware was programmed and no real-board acceptance was performed. Historical v0.10/v0.11 hardware records do not apply to this preview.

menu.smb3_cover: real SMB3 title screen packed as Assets/posters/smb3_title.png; all cover outer border frames removed

build.cover_layout: Cover and rows use 12px side margins (456px wide); title screenshot scaled to 360x272; full_art scaled to 456x360
build.release_hygiene: Duplicate four-game outputs accidentally produced under the old v0.12-preview names were removed. Historical v0.10/v0.11 artifacts were not changed.

implemented: four 8 KiB PRG windows and both PRG modes
1 KiB and 2 KiB CHR banking, even-pair alignment, and inversion
raw CHR and decoded tile pointer updates
PRG RAM enable and write protection in the real 6502 assembly paths
IRQ latch, reload, enable, acknowledge, pending level, and CPU reassertion
8 KiB CHR RAM when the iNES CHR count is zero
mmc3.irq_model: Scanline-level A12 approximation: clock on visible scanlines and the pre-render line when background or sprites are enabled, with identical drawing and draw-skipped timing
limitations: no claim that every Mapper 4 game or all later SMB3 content is compatible

additional_passed_checks: Tests/run_host_tests.sh: ASan/UBSan legacy game and joystick tests plus menu state tests

smb3_real_axf.switch_sequence: SMB3 -> SMB1 -> SMB2 FDS -> SMB3 without mapper, IRQ, SRAM, or dispatch residue

known_unsupported_probe.observed: legacy FDS-conversion PRG-RAM snapshot: four CPU faults and one colour
known_unsupported_probe.reason: This is the explicitly unsupported snapshot path, not the real BIOS/disk-drive path. It was not bypassed or used for SMB2 acceptance; Tests/test_smb2_disk_arm.py passes the supported real-disk boot and gameplay flow.

remaining_real_board_validation: fourth-item menu selection, scrolling, title-screen cover, and return-to-menu behavior on the LCD
SMB3 title, map, level scrolling/status area, controls, and later gameplay on hardware
headphone music/effects, timing, and long-run stability
physical touch Select coordinates and simultaneous-input feel
